what: Machine-readable evidence for the timing, framing and watchdog claims in this repository. Produced by scripts/run_completion_gate.sh from a committed tree. Every number here comes from a simulated in-process CAN bus and a simulated sensor on one Apple Silicon Mac. No CAN hardware, no microcontroller execution, no hardware in the loop, no RTOS.

jitter_us.percentile_reporting: nearest-rank, reported as the upper edge of the containing 10 us bucket. Buckets are half-open, so a reported value r means the true value lies in [r - 10, r). An all-zero run reports every percentile as 10 while max reports 0. min and max are exact.

missed_deadlines.definition: A cycle whose work finished after its own scheduled start plus one period, plus every whole period that elapsed with no cycle executing in it.

control.expected: the positive gate is violated: missed_deadlines > 0 OR p99 jitter > 1000 us

caught_checks.name: positive_gate_fails
caught_checks.expected: false (the gate must not pass under contention)

control.note: Caught. 22 spinning threads (22 with the elevated policy granted) pushed the loop past the frozen deadline gate, which is what makes the gate evidence rather than decoration.

limitations: The CAN bus is simulated in-process. No CAN adapter, transceiver or physical bus was involved, and no frame left this machine.
The sensor is a simulated first-order plant driven by the node's own command. There is no physical sensor and no physical actuator.
This is not hardware in the loop. No device, board, QEMU instance or virtual interface stands in for hardware in these numbers.
Single host. Every number was produced on one Apple Silicon Mac under macOS with other processes running; there is no cross-machine or cross-platform comparison here.

Not a hard real-time system. This is a POSIX-hosted periodic loop with deadline telemetry. The Mach time-constraint policy is requested as a best effort and the grant result is recorded; it is not a guarantee, and macOS may demote the thread.
No RTOS, no ISO 26262 process, no ASIL classification, no automotive qualification and no certification of any kind.

fieldbus-core is compiled for thumbv7em-none-eabihf as a cross-compile check only. It has never been flashed to or executed on a microcontroller, and no timing figure here describes a microcontroller.
The SocketCAN backend uses real AF_CAN sockets but is exercised only against a virtual vcan0 interface on a GitHub Actions ubuntu runner. A virtual interface is a kernel loopback, not a bus.
Jitter percentiles are reported as the upper edge of a 10 us histogram bucket. They are bounds, not exact samples; min and max are exact.
